source.title: The Central Bank Trap
source.summary: Central banks became the bond market's biggest player. Now they can't stop buying without crashing the system, or keep buying without destroying the currency.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: After 2008, the Federal Reserve's balance sheet went from $800 billion to $9 trillion. The Bank of Japan now owns over 50% of all Japanese government bonds. Central banks created trillions of dollars, euros, and yen to buy government debt, and the inflation that followed wasn't a surprise; it was a mathematical certainty. Ibn Taymiyyah condemned currency debasement in the 13th century. Al-Maqrizi analyzed Egypt's monetary crisis in the 15th century. Both understood what modern economists struggle to admit: manipulating the price of money is manipulating the price of everything. This episode examines QE, the Erdogan experiment in Turkey, and the massive hidden wealth transfer from poor to rich.
